questionSimple: I control Magus of the Moon and my opponent plays Dress Down. My opponent has a Breeding Pool (a non-basic land that's a Forest and Island). Does Breeding Pool still tap for green or blue mana?
answerSimple: No. Breeding Pool is a nonbasic Land — Mountain and taps only for {R}. Magus of the Moon's type-changing effect is applied in layer 4, before Dress Down removes Magus's ability in layer 6, so the effect still applies even though Magus has lost its ability. Setting Breeding Pool's land type to Mountain removes Forest, Island and their mana abilities and gives it "{T}: Add {R}". It doesn't change supertypes, so Breeding Pool doesn't become basic.

questionSimple: My Smuggler's Copter has been on the battlefield since the beginning of my turn. I crew it during my combat phase. Can it attack?
answerSimple: Yes, it can attack. Summoning sickness checks whether the permanent has been under your control continuously since the beginning of your most recent turn — it does not check when the permanent became a creature. Smuggler's Copter was already on the battlefield when your turn started, so it has no summoning sickness, and can attack immediately after being crewed.

questionSimple: My opponent casts Trickbind, which has Split Second. While Trickbind is on the stack, can I play a land from my hand?
answerSimple: No, you cannot play a land. Playing a land is a special action and is not a spell or activated ability, so Split Second does not directly prevent it. However, CR 305.1 states that a player may play a land only when the stack is empty. Because Trickbind is on the stack, the precondition for playing a land is not met. You must wait until the stack is empty before playing a land.

questionSimple: My opponent casts Krosan Grip, which has Split Second. In response, can I cast Pact of Negation to counter it? What about Mindbreak Trap?
answerSimple: No. You cannot cast either spell while Split Second is on the stack. Split Second says 'players can't cast other spells' — this applies to all spells, regardless of whether they have an alternative cost, a free cost, or are cast without paying their mana cost. Pact of Negation and Mindbreak Trap are still spells being cast, so Split Second stops them. While a spell with split second is on the stack, players can still activate mana abilities and take special actions (such as turning a face-down creature face up), and triggered abilities still trigger, but no one can cast a spell.
